items.question: Aspirin irreversibly inhibits which enzyme?
items.explanation: Aspirin irreversibly acetylates cyclo-oxygenase (COX), reducing prostaglandins and thromboxane.

items.question: Reye's syndrome in children is linked to which drug in viral fevers?
items.explanation: Aspirin is avoided in children with viral illness due to risk of Reye's syndrome (encephalopathy, hepatic failure).

items.question: Celecoxib has lower GI risk than non-selective NSAIDs but may increase?
items.explanation: Selective COX-2 inhibition reduces protective prostacyclin relative to thromboxane, raising CV risk.

items.question: Why does aspirin cause a prolonged antiplatelet effect lasting ~7-10 days?
options: Irreversible COX-1 acetylation; platelets cannot resynthesise COX
items.explanation: Platelets lack nuclei, so irreversibly inhibited COX cannot be replaced until new platelets form (~7-10 days).

items.question: The ED50 obtained from a quantal dose-response curve measures?
options: Dose effective in 50% of a population
items.explanation: A quantal curve plots the fraction of a population responding; ED50 is the dose effective in 50%.

*PharmaCraft Daily - 01 Nov 2026*

🎓 *MBBS* (Autacoids & NSAIDs)
Q: Aspirin irreversibly inhibits which enzyme?
Ans: Cyclo-oxygenase
Why: Aspirin irreversibly acetylates cyclo-oxygenase (COX), reducing prostaglandins and thromboxane.

🌍 *FMGE* (Autacoids & NSAIDs)
Q: Reye's syndrome in children is linked to which drug in viral fevers?
Ans: Aspirin
Why: Aspirin is avoided in children with viral illness due to risk of Reye's syndrome (encephalopathy, hepatic failure).

🩺 *NEET PG* (Autacoids & NSAIDs)
Q: Celecoxib has lower GI risk than non-selective NSAIDs but may increase?
Ans: Cardiovascular thrombotic events
Why: Selective COX-2 inhibition reduces protective prostacyclin relative to thromboxane, raising CV risk.

🏥 *INI-CET* (Autacoids & NSAIDs)
Q: Why does aspirin cause a prolonged antiplatelet effect lasting ~7-10 days?
Ans: Irreversible COX-1 acetylation; platelets cannot resynthesise COX
Why: Platelets lack nuclei, so irreversibly inhibited COX cannot be replaced until new platelets form (~7-10 days).

🔬 *MD Pharmacology* (Paper I: General/Experimental)
Q: The ED50 obtained from a quantal dose-response curve measures?
Ans: Dose effective in 50% of a population
Why: A quantal curve plots the fraction of a population responding; ED50 is the dose effective in 50%.
